name: isDASTScanScheduled
definition: True when the DAST product holds at least one recurring scan schedule (a recurrence rule with a frequency) that has a next run time and covers at least one site or folder.
population: every scan schedule the DAST product returns to the connected API user (only the sites and folders its groups can see)
evidenceRequiredForTrue: A successful read of the scan schedule list (no GraphQL errors) holding a schedule item with a non-empty RRULE carrying FREQ, a readable next run time (scheduled_run_time) and a non-empty site or folder list. One-off schedules, ended recurrences (no next run) and schedules covering nothing cannot prove it; an unreadable item with no qualifying item is not measured.

openDecisions.question: Should another DAST product (for example a different web application scanner) be allowed to answer this key, or should it stay with Burp Suite DAST until a second implementation is replayed?
positions: any (registered): every Application Security integration may answer it, held to this definition.
listed: only Burp Suite DAST until a second product's implementation is replayed against real data.

citations: safeguards/devsecops/burpsuitedast/isdastscanscheduled.py (reads Integration-Service method listScheduleItems: schedule_items { scheduled_run_time schedule { rrule } sites folders })
https://portswigger.net/burp/extensibility/dast/graphql-api/scheduleitem.html (scheduled_run_time: the next time a scan from this schedule item is due to run; retrieved 2026-11-13)
https://portswigger.net/burp/extensibility/dast/graphql-api/schedule.html (rrule: RFC 5545 recurrence such as FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO; retrieved 2026-11-13)

changeLog.change: Registered for the PortSwigger Burp Suite DAST checks. No live server read yet, so the key is proposed and V0.

notes: An empty schedule list is a fail, not unmeasured: the read succeeded and shows no schedule. If the API user's group does not cover a site, its schedule is invisible; the setup guide says to give the group every site in scope.
